hero.kicker: Fall cleanup and leaf removal in Burton, MI
hero.title: Leaves hauled off, **ditch line included.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes clears Burton yards each fall: leaves blown out of the beds and off the lawn, vacuumed into our trailer and hauled away, perennials cut back and the last mow done. Nothing gets left at the curb waiting for a pickup.

local.title: Leaves off a lawn **that holds water.**
local.intro: In Burton, the leaves should come off before winter. Many lawns here drain slowly, and MSU Extension says leaves left to pile up are hard on the grass beneath them. On wet ground, a mat that sits all winter is the worst case. Leaves raked into a roadside ditch get in the way of the water too.

points.title: Mulch a light fall, remove a heavy one
points.body: MSU Extension says a mower can chop leaves back into the lawn while the layer stays under 3 to 4 inches. Past that, or in the beds and under a big tree, they need to come off, and that is what our vacuum trailer is for.

points.title: Where Burton's yard waste goes
points.body: EMTERRA collects Burton's curbside yard waste. A full cleanup would fill a lot of bags, so what we gather goes straight into our own trailer and leaves with us.

points.title: Burning needs a permit
points.body: Burton requires a permit for any burning, and the city code describes open burning for brush, tree limbs and garden debris, not leaves. Ask the fire department before you light a leaf pile.

points.title: The last mow of the year
points.body: Once the leaves are done and the grass stops growing, MSU Extension suggests lowering the mower no more than one notch, about half an inch, for the final cut. That is how we finish the season.

logistics.title: How a Burton fall cleanup goes.
body: Rob sets a date with you once the trees are mostly bare, and a yard with trees that drop late can get a second pass. The crew blows leaves out of the beds, off the lawn and away from the foundation into rows, then the truck mounted vacuum pulls them into our dump trailer.

Perennials get cut back, beds get raked clean, and the drive and walks are blown off before we go. Where the yard meets a ditch instead of a curb, we pull the leaves out of the ditch line on your side too, so meltwater can drain in spring.
Pair it with a [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup-burton-mi/) and the beds come out of winter ready for [mulch](/mulch-installation-burton-mi/).

faq.q: Do you do leaf removal in Burton?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes does fall cleanups and leaf removal in Burton. We blow the leaves out of beds and off the lawn, vacuum them into our trailer and haul them away, then cut back the beds and blow off the hard surfaces. Rob quotes it free.

faq.q: Is it bad to leave leaves on the lawn all winter?
faq.a: A thick layer, yes. MSU Extension says leaves allowed to pile up are hard on the turf underneath, while a light layer can be chopped back in with a mower. On slow draining Burton lawns, a wet mat left all winter does the most harm.

faq.q: Does Burton pick up leaves at the curb?
faq.a: The city's hauler, EMTERRA, collects yard waste at the curb, and City Hall can tell you your day and the current bag rules. For a whole yard of leaves, a cleanup is simpler, since we take everything away in our own trailer and your cart stays free.

faq.q: When is the last mow of the year in Michigan?
faq.a: When the grass stops growing, usually once the leaves are done. MSU Extension suggests dropping the mower no more than one notch, about half an inch, for that final cut. We fold it into the fall cleanup visit.
